title: How Evidence Attaches to a Relationship

beats.h: How Evidence Attaches to a Relationship
paras: As a graph grows, accurate Nodes stop being enough on their own. The relationship between two Nodes needs to be trustworthy too.
This one line, by itself, doesn't say why the relationship exists. So relationships need evidence too.
A relationship is structure.
Evidence is the material that supports that structure.
A relationship can be thought of as at least two layers:
beats.h: Edge and Evidence Are Different Information
beats.claim: A relationship existing and a relationship being verified are not the same state.

paras: VINC can store evidence and confidence on a relationship.
With evidence in place, the graph moves past just saying "these are connected": it can trace which sentence actually backs that connection.
beats.h: Evidence Can Attach to a Sentence

paras: When a Concept gets extracted from a Document, a link forms between the two.
If that Concept then connects to a Record, another relationship forms.
At that point, it should be possible to trace backward from a final piece of material to where it came from.
This is the core of provenance.
diagrams:
Answer Material
      ↓
Record
      ↓
Concept
      ↓
Document
      ↓
Source Text

paras: Not every relationship carries the same certainty. Some have direct textual support. Some get generated by system structure. Some remain unverified.
So a relationship's existence has to be kept separate from its evidence.
This distinction matters when reading a graph.
If Evidence explains why a connection was made, Confidence expresses how much trust that connection has earned.
Merge the two, and support gets tangled with judgment. So relationship data keeps them as separate fields on purpose.
diagrams:
evidence
= what supports it

confidence
= how much trust is placed in that support

paras: Extracting Concepts from documents, or building graph relationships automatically, is convenient: but automation alone doesn't make a relationship true. A long document title or a vague phrase can end up linked to the wrong Concept.
So generation and verification need to stay separate stages.
This split matters more, not less, as the graph gets more automated.
beats.h: Automatically Generated Relationships Still Need Verification
diagrams:
Source
  ↓
Extraction
  ↓
Candidate Relation
  ↓
Evidence Check
  ↓
Usable Relation

paras: Evidence isn't just a list of sources. It should be possible to trace backward through how a piece of answer material got built.
With this path, an Agent's answer can be reviewed after the fact. Without it (relationships with no evidence) there's no easy way to check the result again.
diagrams:
Question
   ↓
Resolved Node
   ↓
Relation
   ↓
Record
   ↓
Evidence
   ↓
Source Document

paras: Evidence, in the end, doesn't only live in documents. Because a relationship itself can carry evidence, the graph expands from a plain list of connections into a knowledge structure that carries its own support.

This matters again later, once time and View enter the picture. Connect when a relationship was valid, and where it's visible, and the Graph stops being a static structure: it becomes a data structure with time and space built in.
beats.h: Evidence Becomes Part of the Graph
